Trip options

Source: vignettes/articles/trip-options.Rmd
trip-options.Rmd

trip_options() is peabiru’s own trip planner: for each origin and destination it gives every trip worth considering, the ones that no other trip beats on all the chosen criteria at once. Where detailed_itineraries() answers “what is the fastest way there?”, trip_options() answers “what are my choices?”: faster but dearer, cheaper but slower, fewer transfers, less walking.

Not dominated

A trip dominates another when it is no worse on every chosen criterion and better on at least one. The criteria are

  • "TIME": door-to-door minutes from the departure minute, waits included;
  • "FARE": the fare by a fare structure (see vignette("fares"));
  • "TRANSFERS": rides minus one; a trip without public transport has 0, as many as a trip with a single ride;
  • "WALK": minutes on foot: the access and egress legs when they are walked, and the walks between stops (a bicycle or car leg counts 0).

By default all four are used with a fare structure, all but "FARE" without one. At each departure minute of the window the options are the set of trips not dominated, with one trip per combination of values.

The search is exact, to the second. What is returned is then compared at the resolution the values are read at: total time to a tenth of a minute, as it is reported, and walking to the whole minute (rounded half up; walk_resolution sets the step in seconds, and 1 compares the exact seconds). Of the trips of a minute, one is left out when another is no worse on every criterion in those terms and better on one, or equal on all of them and better in exact terms (less total time, then fewer transfers, less walking, a lower fare). Without this, a trip that is slower, dearer and with more transfers would be returned only because it walks a few seconds less. The values reported stay exact. Rounding cannot make a trip look better than one that beats it to the second, so the result is the same as comparing every trip at that resolution.

The trips follow the same network rules as detailed_itineraries() (the same access and egress searches, transfers between stops and boarding rules), so the times agree with the other functions.

The example uses the sample data of Porto Alegre from the r5r project, whose GTFS has timetables, and the fare structure that comes with it, downloaded once into the temporary directory.

poa <- poa_sample()
poa_network <- build_network(poa, n_threads = 2)
fares_zip <- file.path(tempdir(), "fares_poa.zip")
if (!file.exists(fares_zip)) {
  download.file(paste0("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ipea/r5r/v2.5.0/r-package/",
                       "inst/extdata/poa/fares/fares_poa.zip"),
                fares_zip, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
}
fares <- read_fare_structure(fares_zip)
origin <- data.frame(id = "89a90128053ffff", lat = -30.0722552482611, lon = -51.1863771572777)
destination <- data.frame(id = "89a90129c9bffff", lat = -30.0511737750423, lon = -51.1733521719011)

Time and fare

With time and fare as the criteria, the options over the ten minutes from 14:00 trade minutes for reais:

res <- trip_options(poa_network, origin, destination,
                    departure_datetime = departure,
                    criteria = c("TIME", "FARE"), fare_structure = fares,
                    n_threads = 2)
res$options[, c("option", "total_time", "fare", "transfers", "walk_time",
                "departure_time", "n_departures", "description")]
#> # A tibble: 5 × 8
#>   option total_time  fare transfers walk_time departure_time n_departures
#>    <int>      <dbl> <dbl>     <int>     <dbl> <chr>                 <int>
#> 1      1       30.8   7.2         1      16.8 14:05:00                  5
#> 2      2       35.1   4.8         0      24.7 14:05:00                  8
#> 3      3       35.8   7.2         1      20.4 14:00:00                  5
#> 4      4       42.1   4.8         0      33.8 14:07:00                  2
#> 5      5       57.7   0           0      57.7 14:00:00                 10
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: description <chr>

Each row is an option: trips with the same street modes, the same routes between the same stops, and the same fare, transfers and minutes on foot, found at n_departures of the window’s minutes. Its total time changes with the minute (the wait at the start does), so the row reports the trip of its best minute, departure_time. Over the whole window an option can look dominated by another that was not available at its own minutes; by_departure = TRUE adds the frontier of every minute:

res <- trip_options(poa_network, origin, destination,
                    departure_datetime = departure, time_window = 3L,
                    criteria = c("TIME", "FARE"), fare_structure = fares,
                    by_departure = TRUE, itineraries = FALSE, n_threads = 2)
res$departures
#> # A tibble: 9 × 6
#>   from_id         to_id           option departure_time arrival_time total_time
#>   <chr>           <chr>            <int> <chr>          <chr>             <dbl>
#> 1 89a90128053ffff 89a90129c9bffff      1 14:01:00       14:35:48           34.8
#> 2 89a90128053ffff 89a90129c9bffff      1 14:02:00       14:35:48           33.8
#> 3 89a90128053ffff 89a90129c9bffff      2 14:00:00       14:35:48           35.8
#> 4 89a90128053ffff 89a90129c9bffff      3 14:00:00       14:40:03           40.1
#> 5 89a90128053ffff 89a90129c9bffff      3 14:01:00       14:40:03           39.1
#> 6 89a90128053ffff 89a90129c9bffff      3 14:02:00       14:40:03           38.1
#> 7 89a90128053ffff 89a90129c9bffff      4 14:00:00       14:57:40           57.7
#> 8 89a90128053ffff 89a90129c9bffff      4 14:01:00       14:58:40           57.7
#> 9 89a90128053ffff 89a90129c9bffff      4 14:02:00       14:59:40           57.7

All four criteria and the legs

With the default criteria (all four, since there is a fare structure) the trade-offs with transfers and walking come in too. The legs of each option are in itineraries, in the format of detailed_itineraries() and keyed by from_id, to_id and option: an sf of lines, or a table without geometry with drop_geometry = TRUE.

res <- trip_options(poa_network, origin, destination,
                    departure_datetime = departure, fare_structure = fares,
                    drop_geometry = TRUE, n_threads = 2)
nrow(res$options)
#> [1] 4
legs <- res$itineraries
legs[legs$option == 1, c("segment", "mode", "cumulative_fare",
                         "segment_duration", "wait", "distance", "route")]
#> # A tibble: 4 × 7
#>   segment mode  cumulative_fare segment_duration  wait distance route
#>     <int> <chr>           <dbl>            <dbl> <dbl>    <int> <chr>
#> 1       1 WALK              0               10.9   0        694 ""   
#> 2       2 BUS               4.8              7.4   1.2     2113 "T4" 
#> 3       3 BUS               7.2              2.7   2.9     1392 "T1D"
#> 4       4 WALK              7.2              5.8   0        350 ""

max_options keeps the first options of each pair, max_fare and max_trip_duration leave out the trips beyond them, and itineraries = FALSE skips the legs. output_dir writes one CSV file per pair instead.

Fares are not additive

A fare is not the sum of its rides: a transfer within the time allowance is discounted, some types have unlimited transfers, a cap may apply. Two partial trips are only compared on fare when one is at least as cheap for every way both can continue; the comparison makes no assumption about the fare structure (a discounted transfer may even cost more than two full fares). This exactness has a price: partial trips that could still get a discount are kept apart until they cannot, which makes the fare criterion the slowest one.

Frequency-based routes

GTFS frequencies.txt gives a headway, not departure times. The matrix functions draw random departures (Monte Carlo); trip_options() does not: a frequency-based vehicle is boarded at its expected time, half a headway after the traveller is ready to board (or after the period starts), within the period, and with exact_times = 1 at the first scheduled departure. The results do not change from call to call, and differ on purpose from those of the Monte Carlo draws. The Sao Paulo sample shipped with the package runs by frequency:

res <- trip_options(network, points[1, ], points[27, ],
                    departure_datetime = departure, time_window = 5L,
                    itineraries = FALSE, n_threads = 2)
res$options[, c("option", "total_time", "transfers", "walk_time",
                "n_departures", "description")]
#> # A tibble: 6 × 6
#>   option total_time transfers walk_time n_departures description                
#>    <int>      <dbl>     <int>     <dbl>        <int> <chr>                      
#> 1      1       33.1         1      20.4            5 WALK > SUBWAY METRÔ L1 > S…
#> 2      2       33.5         0      24.7            5 WALK > SUBWAY METRÔ L3 > W…
#> 3      3       35.1         1      18.8            5 WALK > SUBWAY METRÔ L1 > B…
#> 4      4       37.5         0      22.7            5 WALK > BUS 2002-10 > WALK  
#> 5      5       54.9         1      17.7            5 WALK > BUS 5290-10 > BUS 2…
#> 6      6       60           2      15.7            5 WALK > BUS 5290-10 > BUS 5…

Compared with the other functions

  • pareto_frontier() gives, for each fare cutoff, the percentiles of the travel time over Monte Carlo draws of departure times: a summary of time against budget, without the trips.
  • detailed_itineraries() gives the fastest trip, or with shortest_path = FALSE the alternatives (one per sequence of routes, the fastest of each).
  • trip_options() gives the trade-offs themselves, trip by trip, with their legs, on any of four criteria. With criteria = "TIME" and time_window = 1, its first option has the total time of detailed_itineraries()’s fastest trip for that minute.
